description: Sites: rfc5280.rs:582-613, oscal/emit.rs:953-994, oscal/parse.rs:909-925, deviation.rs:1009-1066. Every test module in this scope carries a module-level rustdoc block citing its independent oracle: 'openssl x509 -text', 'date -u -d @<unix>', the OSCAL JSON Schema field list, RFC 8398 §3 wording cross-checked with python idna. The test_rfc3339_known_value test even includes the shell command used to verify the expected output 'before commit.' This is the correct discipline for crypto-adjacent tests and the workspace explicitly forbids the alternative (AGENTS.md: 'A test that uses the code under test as its own oracle proves nothing'). A future contributor under deadline pressure will be tempted to assert 'cert.serial_number == cert.serial_number after round-trip' — that pattern proves nothing. The discipline of always citing an external oracle (openssl, pyca, RFC text, hand-computed Punycode) is what makes the test suite meaningful. Defend this against any PR that introduces a test without an oracle comment. The cert_sha256_of test (lib.rs:1877-1898) is particularly well-done: it recomputes the expected hash with sha2 directly outside the lint engine, then compares — that's the right shape.
title: Test discipline — every test cites an independent oracle, not the code under test
